gloss: go out, come forth; (hiphil) bring out, bring forth
summary: To go or come out of a place: out of a house, a city, the ark, the womb, and above all out of Egypt; and so to go out to war, to go out free from service, to come forth by birth from a father’s body, to rise as the sun does, to flow as water and fire do from their source, and of a word, to go forth from the mouth. The hiphil is to bring out, the act that names Yahweh: “I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt” (Exo 20:2), remembered in the booths of the feast (Lev 23:43). The nouns are what goes out and where it goes out from: a going out, an utterance, a spring, the east, the ends of a border, offspring. Akkadian waṣû, Ugaritic and Phoenician yṣʾ, Ge'ez waḍʾa and Sabaic wḍʾ all mean “go out”.

words.gloss: go out, come out, go forth; (hiphil) bring out, bring forth

stems.gloss: go out, come out, go forth

senses.gloss: go out, come out (of a place)
senses.definition: To move from inside a place to outside it: out of the ark, a house, a tent, a city; with מִן and the place left, or לִפְנֵי and the presence left.

evidence.note: “Go out (צֵא) from the ark”; and Noah went out (Gen 8:18).
Lot went out to them at the doorway and shut the door behind him.
Cain went out from the presence of Yahweh.
“Come out, you three, to the tent of meeting”; and the three came out.
The high priest goes out to the altar before Yahweh.
Jeremiah came in and went out among the people, not yet put in prison.
The glory of Yahweh went out from the threshold of the house.

senses.definition: Israel’s going out of Egypt, dated and remembered by that name: the event the feasts were kept to recall and the years were counted from.

evidence.note: “On that very day all the hosts of Yahweh went out (יָצְאוּ) from the land of Egypt.”
“Remember this day on which you went out from Egypt, from the house of slaves.”
Unleavened bread “that you may remember the day of your going out (צֵאתְךָ) from the land of Egypt all the days of your life”.
Time counted from it: “in the third month after the going out (לְצֵאת) of the sons of Israel”.
The temple begun in the 480th year after the sons of Israel went out of Egypt.
“These are the journeys of the sons of Israel who went out of the land of Egypt.”
“As in the days of your going out from the land of Egypt I will show him wonders.”
“When Israel went out from Egypt.”
“Was it not all those who came out (ἐξελθόντες) of Egypt by Moses?”

senses.definition: To go out from the camp or city against an enemy; יֹצֵא צָבָא is a man of age to go out with the host. Yahweh too “goes out” to fight for his people.

evidence.note: “From twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host (כָּל יֹצֵא צָבָא) in Israel.”
“When you go out to battle against your enemies.”
A king to “go out before us and fight our battles”.
Enemies come out against you one way and flee seven ways.
“Yahweh goes out like a mighty man.”
“Then Yahweh will go out and fight against those nations.”
“You went out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of your anointed.”
“You do not go out, God, with our armies.”

senses.gloss: go out and come in (lead, conduct one’s life)
senses.definition: Paired with בּוֹא, the whole of a man’s goings: a leader going out and coming in before the people, and so the conduct of every day.

evidence.note: A man “who will go out before them and come in before them, and who will lead them out and bring them in, that the congregation of Yahweh be not as sheep that have no shepherd”.
All Israel and Judah loved David, “for he went out and came in before them”.
Solomon: “I am a little child; I do not know how to go out or come in.”
Caleb at eighty-five, still strong “for war, and to go out and to come in”.
Moses at a hundred and twenty can no longer go out and come in.
At the word of the priest’s Urim “they shall go out and they shall come in”.
“Blessed shall you be in your coming in and blessed in your going out.”
“Yahweh will keep your going out and your coming in from now and for ever.”

senses.definition: Of a slave, to leave his master’s service; of sold land or a house, to return to its owner in the jubilee.

evidence.note: A Hebrew slave serves six years, “and in the seventh he shall go out free (יֵצֵא לַחָפְשִׁי) for nothing”.
“If he came in single he shall go out single.”
The bondwoman not given her due “shall go out for nothing, without money”.
Sold land “shall go out in the jubilee, and he shall return to his possession”.
The brother who sold himself “shall go out from you, he and his sons with him, and return to his family”.
If not redeemed, “he shall go out in the year of jubilee”.
A house in a walled city, not redeemed in a year, “shall not go out in the jubilee”.

senses.gloss: come forth (by birth, from a father’s body)
senses.definition: To be born: to come out of the womb, and of descendants to come out of a father’s body (“bowels”, “loins”, “thigh”), so that what comes out of a man is his seed.

evidence.note: “This one shall not be your heir, but he who shall come out of your bowels (אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵא מִמֵּעֶיךָ) shall be your heir.”
“I will raise up your seed after you, who shall come out of your bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.”
“Kings shall come out of your loins.”
“All the souls who came with Jacob to Egypt, who came out of his thigh (יֹצְאֵי יְרֵכוֹ).”
“The first came out red”: Esau’s birth; Jacob came out after him (Gen 25:26).
“Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked I shall return there.”
“Before you came out of the womb I set you apart.”
“My son, who came out of my bowels, seeks my life.”
“From you (Bethlehem) shall come out to me one who is to be ruler in Israel.” Quoted at Mat 2:6, ἐκ σοῦ γὰρ ἐξελεύσεται ἡγούμενος.
The scribes quote Mic 5:1 for where the Christ is to be born.
Jacob’s house, “who came out of the waters of Judah”.

senses.definition: Of a shoot or flower, to come up out of the stock or the ground.

evidence.note: “A shoot shall come out (וְיָצָא) from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots shall bear fruit.”
Man “comes forth like a flower and is cut down”.
The hyssop “that comes out in the wall”.

senses.gloss: go out (of breath or soul): die
senses.definition: The soul or breath going out is death itself: the man returns to the ground and his thoughts end.

evidence.note: “As her soul was going out (בְּצֵאת נַפְשָׁהּ), for she died, she called his name Ben-oni.”
“His breath (רוּחוֹ) goes out, he returns to his ground; in that very day his thoughts perish.”
“My soul went out when he spoke”: the bride’s strength fails her.
“Their heart went out”: they lost heart.

senses.gloss: issue, flow out (of water, fire, discharge)
senses.definition: Of water from its source, fire from Yahweh’s presence, and a discharge from the body: to issue out.

evidence.note: “A river went out from Eden to water the garden.”
Strike the rock, “and water shall come out of it”.
Waters going out from under the threshold of the house eastward.
“Living waters shall go out from Jerusalem.”
A spring shall come out of the house of Yahweh.
“Fire went out from before Yahweh and consumed the burnt offering.”
Fire went out from before Yahweh and consumed Nadab and Abihu.
Fire went out from Yahweh against the two hundred and fifty.
“If a man’s emission of seed goes out from him.”
Meat “until it comes out of your nostrils”.

senses.gloss: go forth (of a word, law, decree)
senses.definition: Of speech: to go out of the mouth or lips, and of a command or law, to be issued and take effect.

evidence.note: “So shall my word be that goes out of my mouth: it shall not return to me empty.”
A man who vows “shall do according to all that goes out of his mouth”.
“Out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of Yahweh from Jerusalem.” Also Mic 4:2.
“The word has gone out of my mouth in righteousness and shall not return.”
“At the beginning of your supplications a word went out.”
“Let a royal word go out from before him.”
“Justice never goes forth.”
“Their line has gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.”
Paul applies Psa 19:5 to the preaching: εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτῶν.

senses.gloss: go forth, rise (of sun and stars)
senses.definition: Of the sun, to come up over the earth; of stars, to come out at nightfall.

evidence.note: “The sun had gone out over the earth when Lot came to Zoar.”
The sun, “like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber”.
“Let those who love him be like the going out of the sun in its might.”
From dawn “until the stars came out”.

senses.definition: Of a lot, to come out for a tribe or a man, so deciding the matter.

evidence.note: “Wherever the lot comes out for him, that shall be his.”
“The second lot came out for Simeon.”
“The first lot came out for Jehoiarib.”

senses.definition: Of a boundary line, to run out to a point on its course.

evidence.note: Judah’s border “went out to the south of the ascent of Akrabbim”.
“It shall go out to Hazar-addar.”
“And came out at the Jordan.”

senses.gloss: come out (of trouble), escape; come out (as the result)
senses.definition: To come out from a danger or a charge, free of it; and to come out at the end of a process as its result.

evidence.note: “The righteous comes out of trouble.”
Saul and Jonathan were taken by the lot, “and the people went out”: cleared.
“He who fears God shall come out of them all.”
Evil “which they shall not be able to come out of”.
“Take away the dross from the silver, and there comes out a vessel for the refiner.”
“When he has tried me, I shall come out as gold.”

stems.gloss: bring out, lead out; bring forth

senses.gloss: bring out, lead out (of Egypt, of bondage)
senses.definition: To lead persons out of a place, above all Yahweh’s bringing Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves: the act by which he names himself and claims them as his.

evidence.note: “I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out (הוֹצֵאתִיךָ) of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves.”
“That your generations may know that I made the sons of Israel dwell in booths when I brought them out (בְּהוֹצִיאִי) of the land of Egypt: I am Yahweh your God.”
“Who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God: I am Yahweh.”
“They are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; they shall not be sold as slaves are sold.”
“To me the sons of Israel are servants … whom I brought out of the land of Egypt.”
“Who brought you out … that you should not be their slaves; I broke the bars of your yoke.”
“I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.”
“By strength of hand Yahweh brought you out from this place.”
“Not like the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt”, quoted at Heb 8:9.
Quoting Jer 31:32: ἐξαγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου.
Stephen: “He brought them out (ἐξήγαγεν), having done wonders and signs in Egypt.”
A leader “who will lead them out and bring them in”.
“I am Yahweh who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans.”
“I will bring you out from the peoples” in a second exodus.

senses.gloss: bring out, carry out (persons or things)
senses.definition: To take something or someone outside: bread brought out to a guest, a carcass carried outside the camp, an offender brought out to be stoned.

evidence.note: “Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine.”
The whole bull of the sin offering he “shall carry out to outside the camp” and burn.
The bull and goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to cover in the holy place, “shall be carried out to outside the camp”; cited at Heb 13:11–12.
“The bodies of those animals whose blood is brought into the holy places … are burned outside the camp”; so Jesus suffered outside the gate (Heb 13:12).
“Bring out the one who cursed to outside the camp”; they did so (Lev 24:23).
The sabbath-breaker brought outside the camp and stoned.
“Bring out to me these five kings from the cave.”
“You shall not carry any of the flesh outside the house.”

senses.gloss: bring forth (produce, as earth and plant do; the stars, the wind)
senses.definition: Of the earth or a plant, to put forth what grows from it; of Yahweh, to bring out the stars by number and the wind from his storehouses.

evidence.note: On the third day “the earth brought forth (וַתּוֹצֵא) grass, plant yielding seed after its kind”, as God had said.
On the sixth day: “Let the earth bring forth the living soul after its kind.”
Aaron’s rod “brought forth buds, bloomed blossoms and yielded almonds”.
“To bring forth bread from the earth.”
“As the earth brings forth its sprouts.”
“On what the ground brings forth.”
“Who created these? He who brings out their host by number, who calls them all by name.”
“Can you bring out Mazzaroth in its season?”
“He brings out the wind from his storehouses.” Also Jer 10:13.

senses.definition: To bring words out of the mouth, a report into the open, or justice to the nations.

evidence.note: “Behold my servant … he will bring forth justice (מִשְׁפָּט … יוֹצִיא) to the nations”; quoted of Jesus at Mat 12:18.
“He will bring forth justice in truth”; Mat 12:20 renders “until he brings out (ἐκβάλῃ) justice to victory”.
Matthew’s rendering of Isa 42:3.
“They brought out an evil report of the land.” Also Num 14:36–37.
“He who brings out slander is a fool.”
“A fool brings out all his spirit.”
“Let not your heart hurry to bring out a word before God.”
“Shall they not bring out words from their heart?”
“He will bring forth your righteousness as the light.”
“If you bring out the precious from the worthless, you shall be as my mouth.”

senses.definition: To bring someone out of trouble, prison, a net or darkness: to deliver.

evidence.note: “He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death and burst their bands.”
“Bring my soul out of prison.”
“To bring out the prisoner from the dungeon.”
“He will bring my feet out of the net.”
“He brought them out of their distresses.”
“He brought me out into a broad place.”
“He will bring me out to the light.”

senses.definition: To cause foreign wives and their children to go out of the household.

evidence.note: “Let us make a covenant with our God to put away (לְהוֹצִיא) all the wives and those born of them.”
They gave their hand to put away their wives.

senses.definition: To bring money out of the treasury or levy it from the people.

evidence.note: “Menahem exacted (וַיֹּצֵא) the money from Israel, from all the mighty men of wealth, fifty shekels each.”
The money was paid out (וַיּוֹצִיאֻהוּ) to the carpenters and builders of the house of Yahweh.

senses.definition: To be led or brought out by another.

evidence.note: Tamar “was being brought out (מוּצֵאת)” to be burned when she sent to her father-in-law.
The women of the king’s house “being brought out” to the princes of the king of Babylon.
Survivors “who are brought out”, sons and daughters.
The land of Israel, gathered from many peoples: “it has been brought out from the peoples”.
The waters issuing to the sea, “the waters brought out”; the sense of הַמּוּצָאִים here is not certain.

evidence.locator: Exo.12.41, יָצְאוּ → ἐξῆλθεν; Isa.55.11, יֵצֵא → ἐξέλθῃ; Mic.5.1, יֵצֵא → ἐξελεύσεται; ἐξέρχομαι renders יָצָא ×446

evidence.note: Mic 5:1: “out of you shall come forth (ἐξελεύσεται) a ruler”.
Psa 19:5: “their voice went out (ἐξῆλθεν) into all the earth”.
Isa 52:11: “Come out (ἐξέλθατε) from their midst and be separate.”
“Come out of her, my people”, after Jer 51:45, צְאוּ מִתּוֹכָהּ עַמִּי.
Those who came out (ἐξελθόντες) of Egypt by Moses.
Abraham obeyed “to go out (ἐξελθεῖν) to a place he was to receive”, as Gen 12:4–5.

evidence.locator: Exo.20.2, הוֹצֵאתִיךָ → ἐξήγαγον; Exo.13.3, הוֹצִיא → ἐξήγαγεν; ἐξάγω renders יָצָא ×98

evidence.note: Jer 31:32: “to lead them out (ἐξαγαγεῖν) of the land of Egypt”.
Moses “led them out (ἐξήγαγεν)”.
“This Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt.”
“With an uplifted arm he led them out of it.”

evidence.locator: Exo.19.1, לְצֵאת → τῆς ἐξόδου; Exo.23.16; Num.33.38; 1Ki.6.1 the same: ἔξοδος renders the infinitive צֵאת ×7

evidence.note: Moses and Elijah spoke with Jesus of “his ἔξοδος which he was about to fulfil at Jerusalem”: his going out, his death.
Joseph, dying, made mention of the ἔξοδος of the sons of Israel.
Peter of his own death: “after my ἔξοδος”.

evidence.locator: Gen.1.12, וַתּוֹצֵא → ἐξήνεγκεν; Isa.42.1 and 42.3, יוֹצִיא → ἐξοίσει; ἐκφέρω renders יָצָא ×39

evidence.note: Ground “bearing (ἐκφέρουσα) thorns and briers”, the earth’s bringing forth as in Gen 1:12.

opposites.note: “Come in”, its pair: going out and coming in is the whole of a man’s goings.
“Return”: a word goes out and does not return empty; a man comes out of the womb and returns naked.

parallels.note: “Go up”: the exodus is told as both Israel’s going out and its going up from Egypt.

phrases.gloss: bring out of the land of Egypt
one who goes out with the host: of age for war
those who came out of his thigh: his descendants

words.gloss: going out; what goes out (utterance); place of going out: spring, east, source
words.summary: A noun of place and act formed with מ: the going out itself, what goes out (a word from the lips, horses exported), and where something goes out from (a spring, the sun’s rising, a mine). The proper name Moza (1Ch 2:46; 8:36–37; 9:42–43) shares the spelling and is left to a name entry.

senses.definition: The act of going out, a stage of departure on a journey, and the way out of a building.

evidence.note: “Moses wrote their goings out (מוֹצָאֵיהֶם) by their journeys at the command of Yahweh.”
Abner came “to know your going out (מוֹצָאֲךָ) and your coming in (מוֹבָאֶךָ)”.
“You shall go out at evening in their sight, like the goings out of exiles.”
The house’s “exits and its entrances (מוֹצָאָיו וּמוֹבָאָיו)”.
“The going out of the horses which Solomon had was from Egypt”: their export. Also 2Ch 1:16.

senses.gloss: what goes out of the mouth: utterance, word
senses.definition: What goes out of the lips or mouth: a vow spoken, a promise, the word by which Yahweh gives life.

evidence.note: “Man does not live by bread alone, but by everything that goes out of the mouth (מוֹצָא פִי) of Yahweh does man live”; quoted at Mat 4:4, ἐπὶ παντὶ ῥήματι ἐκπορευομένῳ διὰ στόματος θεοῦ.
Jesus answers with Deu 8:3 in the wilderness.
“All that went out of her lips (מוֹצָא שְׂפָתֶיהָ) for her vows … shall not stand.”
“What has gone out of your lips you shall keep and do.”
“I will not profane my covenant, nor change what has gone out of my lips”: the oath to David.
“What came out of my lips was before your face.”
“From the going forth of the word (מֹצָא דָבָר) to restore and to build Jerusalem until an anointed one, a prince”: the issuing of a decree.

senses.gloss: going forth of the sun: rising, east; dawn
senses.definition: Where and when the sun goes out: its rising, the east; the going forth of morning.

evidence.note: “Not from the going out (מִמּוֹצָא) nor from the west (מִמַּעֲרָב)”: east set against west.
The sun: “its going out is from the end of the heavens, and its circuit to their ends.”
Yahweh’s “going forth is sure as the dawn”.
“The goings out of morning and evening you make to shout for joy.”

senses.gloss: source, spring (of water); source of ore
senses.definition: The place water goes out from the ground; a spring; and the place silver comes from.

evidence.note: Elisha “went out to the spring of the waters (מוֹצָא הַמַּיִם) and threw salt in it”.
“Like a watered garden, and like a spring of water whose waters do not fail.”
“The dry land springs of water.”
He turns “springs of water into thirsty ground”; and the reverse (Psa 107:35).
Hezekiah stopped “the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon”.
“To make the source of grass (מֹצָא דֶשֶׁא) spring up.”
“There is a source (a mine) for silver, and a place for gold which they refine.”

evidence.locator: Ezk.12.4, מוֹצָאֵי → ἐκπορεύεται; Psa.19.6, יֹצֵא → ἐκπορευόμενος; ἐκπορεύομαι renders יָצָא ×99

evidence.note: Deu 8:3: “by every word that goes out (ἐκπορευομένῳ) of the mouth of God”.
“What goes out (ἐκπορευόμενον) of the mouth, this defiles a man.”

opposites.note: “Entrance, coming in”, beside it of a man’s goings and of the house’s ways.

phrases.gloss: what goes out of the mouth of Yahweh
what goes out of the lips: a spoken vow or promise

words.gloss: outgoings: end of a border; way out, escape; source
words.summary: Only in the plural: where something goes out to or from. Most uses are the far ends of a border in Numbers and Joshua; once the outlets of a city, once escape from death, once the outgoings of life from the heart.

senses.gloss: outgoings, far ends (of a border, a territory)
senses.definition: Where a boundary line runs out and ends; the farthest reaches of a land.

evidence.note: “Its outgoings (תּוֹצְאֹתָיו) shall be south of Kadesh-barnea.”
“Its outgoings shall be at the sea.”
“The outgoings of the border were at the sea: this shall be your south border.”
The forest hill country: “you shall cut it down, and its outgoings shall be yours”, to its farthest extent.
Gad dwelt in the pasturelands of Sharon “to their outgoings”.

senses.definition: The ways out of the city, its gates, measured by side.

evidence.note: “These are the outgoings of the city”: on each side its measure and three gates (Ezk 48:31).

senses.definition: A way of going out from danger: escape.

evidence.note: “Our God is a God of salvations, and to Yahweh the Lord belong the ways out (תּוֹצָאוֹת) from death.”

senses.definition: What goes out of the heart: the springs from which a man’s life and conduct flow.

evidence.note: “Keep your heart above all keeping, for out of it are the outgoings of life (תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים).”

evidence.locator: Num.34.4, תּוֹצְאֹתָיו → διέξοδος; Jos.15.4 and the border lists the same; Psa.68.21 → διέξοδοι

evidence.note: “Go to the outlets (διεξόδους) of the roads”, where they run out of the city.

words.summary: Only in the plural: what comes out of a man, his descendants, almost always beside זֶרַע “seed”; and what comes out of the earth, its produce. Formed by repeating the root’s last two letters.

senses.definition: Those who have come out of a man’s body, set beside his seed.

evidence.note: “Your seed would have been like the sand, and the offspring of your bowels (צֶאֱצָאֵי מֵעֶיךָ) like its grains.”
“I will pour my spirit on your seed, and my blessing on your offspring.”
“Their seed shall be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples.”
“The seed of the blessed of Yahweh, and their offspring with them.”
“Your seed shall be many, and your offspring as the grass of the earth.”
The wicked man’s offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.
On Eliakim they hang all the glory of his father’s house, “the offspring and the issue”.

senses.definition: What comes out of the ground: its growth and crops.

evidence.note: Yahweh “who spread out the earth and what comes out of it (וְצֶאֱצָאֶיהָ)”.
“Let the earth hear and its fulness, the world and all that comes out of it.”
“Let me sow and another eat, and let my produce be rooted out.”

parallels.note: “Seed”, beside it in almost every use.

words.gloss: origin, going forth; place to go out to (privy)
words.summary: Twice, both plural: the ruler’s “goings out” from of old (Mic 5:1), and, in the read text of 2Ki 10:27, the house of Baal made into a place for going out, a privy.

senses.gloss: goings out, origins (of the ruler from Bethlehem)
senses.definition: Where the coming ruler comes out from: his descent, set from days long past.

evidence.note: “From you shall come out (יֵצֵא) to me one who is to be ruler in Israel, and his goings out (וּמוֹצָאֹתָיו) are from of old, from days of antiquity (מִימֵי עוֹלָם).” The verb in the same verse is his birth from Bethlehem.
The seed promised to David “who shall come out of your bowels”.
In Micah “from days of old (מִימֵי קֶדֶם)” is the time of the oath to the fathers.

senses.definition: A place to go out to: the qere’s word for a latrine.

evidence.note: Jehu’s men broke down the house of Baal “and made it into לְמוֹצָאוֹת to this day”: the qere, for the written לְמַחֲרָאוֹת, “privies”.

words.summary: Once, in the written text of 2Ch 32:21, of the sons who had come out of Sennacherib’s body; a verbal adjective of the qal’s “come forth by birth”.

senses.definition: Sons, as those who have come out of their father.

evidence.note: In the house of his god “some of those who came out of his bowels (וּמִיצִיאֵי מֵעָיו) struck him down with the sword” (written ומיציאו); 2Ki 19:37 names them his sons.

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, once: a shaphel “bring out” in the sense “bring to its end, finish”. Aramaic has its own verb for going out (נְפַק); this one answers to Akkadian šūṣû, the causative of waṣû, and is taken to have come into Aramaic from it.

senses.definition: To bring a work to its end, of the house of God rebuilt after the exile.

evidence.note: “And this house was finished (וְשֵׁיצִיא) on the third day of the month Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.”

cognates.gloss: go out, come out, leave, escape, rise, grow, be uttered; (Š) bring out, send out, release
cognates.note: The Akkadian verb covers nearly every use of the Hebrew: going out of a place, escaping, coming forth, rising, growing, being uttered, and in the causative bringing out and setting free. The Š-stem šūṣû is the source of Aramaic שֵׁיצִיא.

cognates.gloss: going out, exit, departure; rising, sunrise, east; offspring, birth; place of origin; utterance; issue, expenditure
cognates.note: The Akkadian noun of going out gathers the senses of the Hebrew nouns: the sun’s rising and the east (מוֹצָא, Psa 19:7; 75:7), utterance (מוֹצָא שְׂפָתַיִם), place of origin (מוֹצָאָה, Mic 5:1), and offspring (צֶאֱצָא).

cognates.gloss: go out, come out; come forth (to battle); rise (of the sun); spend
cognates.note: Phoenician and Punic: men coming out of a place (Plautus’ Poenulus), enemies coming out to fight (CIS i 91; the Kition inscription), as the Hebrew “go out to battle”.

cognates.note: The Karatepe inscription’s “from the going out of the sun to its going in” (KAI 26 A I 4–5) is the same noun of place as Hebrew מוֹצָא for the sun’s rising and the east (Psa 19:7; 75:7).

cognates.gloss: go out, come out, depart; come forth, be born; go out free; flow; rise (of the sun); come out (of a lot); sprout; be uttered; (causative አውፅአ) bring out
cognates.note: Ge'ez ፅ (ḍ) shows the older lateral ṣ́ behind צ. Dillmann’s senses, drawn from the Ge'ez Bible and other texts, run parallel to the Hebrew: go out to war, emigrate, be born, go out free, flow, rise of the sun and stars, come out of a lot, sprout, be uttered.

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic noun from the shaphel verb שֵׁיצִי “finish, bring to an end”, used in the Targum of Proverbs for an end that comes on the fool (Targ. Prov 10:14, 29; 18:7). It shows the Aramaic verb of Ezr 6:15 in its own use.

evidence.locator: s.v. שֵׁיצְיָא

cognates.gloss: burst forth, bloom; (aphel) let burst forth, utter
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, in the Targum for Hebrew פָּרַח of Aaron’s rod (Targ. O. Num 17:23) and with an aphel “utter”. Aramaic writes ע for the older ṣ́ (as in אַרְעָא for אֶרֶץ), so יְעָא could be the same root as יָצָא, matching the hiphil of the budding rod (Num 17:23) and the uttered word; possible only, since no Aramaic text uses it for “go out”.

evidence.locator: s.v. יְעָא
evidence.note: Targ. O. Num. 17:23 (Heb. פרח); Af. Targ. Prov. 10:31; Targ. Ps. 19:3.

cognates.gloss: be fair, clean, neat; (V) perform ablution
cognates.note: The Arabic root with the expected consonants (w-ḍ-ʾ) means “be clean, comely”, not “go out”, and Arabic uses other roots (خرج) for going out. Its tie to יָצָא rests on the sounds alone; no Hebrew word is named with it.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh names himself by this act: “I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves” (Exo 20:2), and the law repeats it as the ground of its commands (Lev 22:33; 26:13). Because he brought them out, they are his servants and may not be sold as slaves (Lev 25:42, 55). The feasts were kept so that the going out would be remembered: unleavened bread “all the days of your life” (Deu 16:3; Exo 13:3), and the booths, so that the generations would know he made Israel dwell in booths when he brought them out (Lev 23:43). Hebrews says that coming out was not enough: those who came out of Egypt by Moses fell in the wilderness for unbelief (Heb 3:16–19), and the new covenant is “not like” the one made on the day he brought them out (Jer 31:32; Heb 8:9). Luke calls Jesus’ death at Jerusalem his ἔξοδος (Luk 9:31), the word the Septuagint uses for Israel’s going out of Egypt (Exo 19:1). From the verses: the going out of Egypt is the pattern of redemption, a people taken out of bondage to belong to Yahweh, and the New Testament sets Christ’s death as the going out by which the new covenant is made.

When Rachel’s soul was “going out” it is explained “for she died” (Gen 35:18), and the psalm says of man: “his breath goes out, he returns to his ground; in that very day his thoughts perish” (Psa 146:4). Job sets the two ends of life side by side: naked he came out of his mother’s womb and naked he will return (Job 1:21). The verses describe the going out of soul or breath as the man’s death and his return to the ground, with his thoughts ended that day, not as a conscious self leaving to live elsewhere.

The verb is the word for a son’s coming out of his father: Abraham’s heir “shall come out of your bowels” (Gen 15:4), kings “shall come out of your loins” (Gen 35:11), and David’s seed, whose kingdom Yahweh will establish, is the one “who shall come out of your bowels” (2Sa 7:12). Isaiah’s shoot “comes out” of the stump of Jesse (Isa 11:1). Micah says of Bethlehem, “from you shall come out to me one who is to be ruler in Israel, and his goings out (מוֹצָאֹת) are from of old, from days of antiquity” (Mic 5:1), and Matthew gives the verse as the place of the Christ’s birth (Mat 2:6). Micah himself uses “the days of antiquity” and “the days of old” of Israel’s past and of the oath sworn to the fathers (Mic 7:14, 20). From the verses: the ruler’s “goings out” are his descent, out of Judah and David’s line, promised and traced from the days of the fathers; his coming out is his birth at Bethlehem, not a life before it.

Isaiah calls the exiles to leave Babylon: “Depart, depart, go out from there, touch no unclean thing; go out from her midst, be clean, you who carry the vessels of Yahweh” (Isa 52:11), and Jeremiah: “Go out from her midst, my people, and each save his soul from the fierce anger of Yahweh” (Jer 51:45; also Jer 50:8). Paul applies Isa 52:11 to the believers at Corinth and their separation from idols: “Come out from their midst and be separate” (2Co 6:16–17), and the call to come out of Babylon is repeated at Rev 18:4. From the verses: the call to go out of Babylon is a call to Yahweh’s people in every age to leave what is unclean and idolatrous before its judgment falls.

What goes out of Yahweh’s mouth does what he sent it to do: “it shall not return to me empty” (Isa 55:11; also Isa 45:23), and what has gone out of his lips he will not change (Psa 89:35). Man lives “by everything that goes out of the mouth of Yahweh” (Deu 8:3), the answer Jesus gives in the wilderness (Mat 4:4), and the law and the word of Yahweh are to go out from Zion to the nations (Isa 2:3). The same holds of a man’s own word: what has gone out of his lips in a vow he must keep (Num 30:3; Deu 23:24).

note: Moza (מוֹצָא, BDB j.cq.ae: Caleb’s son 1Ch 2:46; Saul’s descendant 1Ch 8:36–37; 9:42–43) is a proper name of this root and is left to a name entry; its key is not claimed here. Its tokens are also filed under j.cq.ad, which this entry claims, so the noun’s count includes the name. The place Mozah (הַמֹּצָה, Jos 18:26) is spelled differently and is a place, not a person. The brief lists εὑρίσκω as a Greek loan via מָצָא: that is another root (מצא “find”) and is not recorded. The brief files 2Sa 18:4 יָצְאוּ under the verb by spelling but analyses it as ירד; left as is. Ge'ez is cited from Dillmann only; Leslau’s Comparative Dictionary (waḍʾa) not yet checked. CAD A/2 (aṣû) not yet checked by page. Sabaic cited from Biella; SabaWeb root wḍʾ not checked. The Aramaic verb שֵׁיצִיא is treated as a loan from Akkadian šūṣû on Segert’s note; Jastrow’s verb entry is missing from the vendored Sefaria file (only the noun שֵׁיצְיָא is there). Arabic وضؤ and Aramaic יְעָא are possible cognates by sound only. Hophal Ezk 47:8 הַמּוּצָאִים is obscure. Doctrine messiah-origin states the descent reading of Mic 5:1 plainly; for the reviewer to check.
